notes: Founder; tenure predates the window. His last show, on the haute couture schedule and his first show in six years, was at his Paris gallery on Wednesday 2017-07-05 (FashionUnited schedule 2017-06-30; photo caption via Ebony); it is kept although shown in couture week because Alaïa showed off the ready-to-wear calendar. Died 2017-11-18; the Fédération de la Haute Couture announced the death that Saturday (AP via Arab News), so left_announced_date is the date of death. The house said his final ready-to-wear designs would be shown in Paris in January and March 2018 (FashionUnited 2017-12-18); those were not runway shows checked here.

In-house team after the founder's death; announced_date is the house statement of 2017-12-18 that the Alaïa team would stay with the house (FashionUnited). No runway show in this period: Mulier's July 2021 show was described as the first Alaïa runway presentation since 2017 (FashionNetwork 2021-05-20). Ended when Richemont named Pieter Mulier (release dated Paris, 2021-02-05).

Named creative director effective immediately, first collection to be Spring Summer 22 (Richemont release, Paris, 2021-02-05). Debut show, ready-to-wear and couture together, rue de Moussy, Paris, Sunday 2021-07-04 at 21:00 on the eve of couture week (FashionNetwork 2021-05-20; FashionUnited 2021-07-05). Exit confirmed Friday 2026-01-30 (The Impression; FashionNetwork). Last show, the collection the house called Summer-Fall 2026 (reported as Fall/Winter 2026), Fondation Cartier, Paris, Wednesday 2026-03-04 (FashionUnited and W, both 2026-03-05, say 'Wednesday'). Then joined Versace (see versace rows).

On 2026-01-30 Alaïa said the studio would ensure continuity until a new creative organisation is confirmed (The Impression). SS27 was designed by the house studio and shown as a presentation, not a runway, in Paris on Saturday 2026-10-03 from 18:00 per the published calendar (Grazia 2026-07-30; Fashion Week Daily 2026-08-03); a post-event report (2026-10-05) confirms the studio presentation took place but does not restate the date. No successor named as of 2026-10-06 (W).

Artistic director since 1997 (FashionNetwork); appointment announcement and first show dates not confirmed, left blank. Last show SS13, Paris, Thursday 27 Sep 2012 (AFP review published 28 Sep). Balenciaga and Ghesquière announced on 5 Nov 2012 their joint decision to end the relationship as of 30 Nov 2012.

Creative director. Balenciaga and PPR confirmed the appointment on 3 Dec 2012. First show AW13, Paris, Thursday 28 Feb 2013. Exit was first reported by US media on 29 Jul 2015 (unconfirmed by Balenciaga that day); the joint statement announcing non-renewal was published 31 Jul 2015 and said his last show would be SS16 womenswear on 2 Oct 2015 in Paris, which NOWFASHION confirms.

Appointed as Demna Gvasalia (artistic director), 7 Oct 2015. First show AW16 womenswear, Paris, Sunday 6 Mar 2016; he also designed menswear (menswear show dates not checked). Exit implied by Kering's announcement of his Gucci appointment on Thursday 13 Mar 2025; no separate Balenciaga statement date confirmed. Last show: 54th haute couture collection, Paris, Wednesday 9 Jul 2025; his last ready-to-wear show was AW25 in March 2025 (date not checked here).

Creative director (house-wide; scope 'both' assumed from the title, not checked line by line). Kering announced on Monday 19 May 2025; he started 10 Jul 2025. First show SS26 at the Hôpital Laennec, rue de Sèvres, Saturday 4 Oct 2025, 20:00. No departure found; current status checked only against Wikipedia, not against an SS27 show report.

Creative director from June 2001 (Wikipedia); appointment announcement and first show dates not confirmed, left blank. Last show AW18, shown in New York on 10 Feb 2018 (NOWFASHION show listing). Exit date from Wikipedia only ('Kering announced Maier's resignation on 13 June 2018', citing a New York Times article of that date that could not be read), hence verified=false.

Appointed June 2018 (Wikipedia; its source is a British Vogue report dated 15 Jun 2018); exact announcement date not confirmed, left blank. First show AW19, Milan, 23 Feb 2019 (NOWFASHION). His last show on the Milan calendar per NOWFASHION was AW20, 22 Feb 2020; no later show is listed and the date of his final collection was not confirmed, so last_show_date is blank. Exit date 10 Nov 2021 is from Wikipedia only.

Appointed November 2021 (Wikipedia); exact announcement date not confirmed, left blank. First show AW22, Milan, 26 Feb 2022 (NOWFASHION). Last show SS25, Milan, Saturday 21 Sep 2024, 20:00 (The Impression calendar; review the same day). Kering announced his exit and Louise Trotter's appointment on Thursday 12 Dec 2024, about an hour before Chanel named him.

Kering press release Thursday 12 Dec 2024; she joined at the end of January 2025. First show SS26, Milan, Saturday 27 Sep 2025, 17:00 (The Impression calendar and Vogue Philippines schedule; NOWFASHION lists the same date). The Impression's review is timestamped 26 Sep, which looks pre-dated; the project registry's 28 Sep disagrees with all three listings. Still in post: AW26 reviewed 2 Mar 2026; NOWFASHION lists SS27 on 26 Sep 2026.

Founder; tenure predates the window, so all date fields are blank by design. Listed as Executive Chairman and Creative Director on the company's board page (board appointed 2026-04-23); AW26 described as his work (FashionNetwork 2026-03-01). The house presents collections rather than staging runway shows. Daughters hold creative roles under him: Camilla Cucinelli (listed as Co-Head Women's Creative Director) and Carolina Cucinelli (Co-Creative Director), both given product and image powers in March 2024 and made Vice Presidents in July 2024; Giovanna Manfredi is co-creative director of the women's style office. Not treated as a change of creative lead; appointment dates for the daughters' creative titles were not found.

Joined May 2001, creative director from 2004, chief creative officer from November 2009, also CEO 2014 to 2017 (Wikipedia); start dates not filled. Last show AW18, London, 17 Feb 2018 (NOWFASHION). Exit announcement date not confirmed (Wikipedia cites a New York Times report of 31 Oct 2017), left blank.

Chief creative officer. Appointed March 2018 and replaced in September 2022 (Wikipedia, citing WWD of 1 Mar 2018 and BoF of 28 Sep 2022); exact announcement dates not confirmed, left blank. First show SS19, London, 17 Sep 2018 (NOWFASHION). His last show (SS23, London, September 2022) is not listed by NOWFASHION and its date was not confirmed, left blank; the last show of his that NOWFASHION lists is AW22, 11 Mar 2022.

Chief creative officer. Appointed September 2022 (Wikipedia); exact announcement date not confirmed, left blank. First show AW23, London, 20 Feb 2023 (NOWFASHION; Wikipedia says his debut was AW23). No departure found: Wikipedia (updated May 2026) describes him as in post and NOWFASHION lists SS27 on 21 Sep 2026.

Appointment date from Wikipedia only (citing a WWD report of 4 Sep 2008). First show SS10, Paris, 5 Oct 2009, and last runway show SS18, Paris, 1 Oct 2017 (both NOWFASHION, which names Philo). Wikipedia says she announced her exit in December 2017; exact date not confirmed, left blank. Wikipedia pages disagree on whether her last collection was Pre-Fall 2018 or an AW18 collection presented in March 2018; NOWFASHION lists no Celine AW18 show, and no design-studio show between her exit and Slimane's debut was confirmed.

Artistic, creative and image director, women's and men's. Appointment date from Wikipedia only (citing LVMH's BusinessWire release of 21 Jan 2018; the release page did not load). First show SS19, Paris, 28 Sep 2018 (NOWFASHION); first standalone menswear show AW19, 20 Jan 2019 (NOWFASHION; Wikipedia). Last show not confirmed: NOWFASHION's last listing of his era is SS23 menswear at the Palais de Tokyo, 26 Jun 2022, and later collections were not found in a source read here. Exit reported October 2024 (Wikipedia cites Vogue Business, 2 Oct 2024); exact announcement date not confirmed.

Named creative director in early October 2024 (Wikipedia cites Vogue Business, 2 Oct 2024); exact announcement date not confirmed, left blank; joined early 2025. Debut (SS26, men's and women's together) was shown in Celine's rue Vivienne showrooms, Paris, just before the couture week that opened Monday 7 Jul 2025 (AnOther, 7 Jul and 6 Oct 2025); The Impression's review is timestamped 6 Jul 2025. The 6 Jul date is inferred from these, not stated in them. NOWFASHION's Celine SS26 page is dated 30 Sep 2025, which looks like a gallery timestamp. Still in post as far as checked (Wikipedia; NOWFASHION lists AW26 on 7 Mar 2026; LVMH posted a Celine SS27 show item on 6 Oct 2026).

Appointment announcement date not confirmed, left blank; FashionNetwork says he took up the reins in January 1983 and Dazed gives his first show as 25 Jan 1983 at 31 rue Cambon. Died 19 Feb 2019; Chanel named Virginie Viard the same day. Last collection AW19 shown posthumously on Tuesday 5 Mar 2019 at the Grand Palais, the first programme credited to Karl Lagerfeld and Virginie Viard.

First collection solely hers: Cruise 2020 at the Grand Palais, 3 May 2019. She co-signed Lagerfeld's last collection (AW19, 5 Mar 2019) and took that bow. Last show she presented: Cruise 2024/25 on the Cité Radieuse rooftop, Marseille, Thursday 2 May 2024 (date from Chanel's show announcement; review published 3 May). Exit announced late Wednesday 5 Jun 2024. Couture AW24 (25 Jun 2024) was billed in advance as her last collection but was completed by the in-house team and shown without her, so it is counted under the design studio row.

Chanel in-house studio after Viard's exit, no named lead. First show Couture AW24 at the Palais Garnier, Tuesday 25 Jun 2024 (completed by the in-house team; begun under Viard). Last show Couture AW25 at the Grand Palais, Tuesday 8 Jul 2025, described by FashionNetwork as the last of seven collections by the in-house studio. No appointment announcement, so announced_date is blank; left_announced_date is the day Matthieu Blazy's appointment was announced.

Title: artistic director of fashion activities. Announced 12 Dec 2024, about an hour after Kering announced his exit from Bottega Veneta. First show SS26, Paris, 6 Oct 2025 (FHCM official collection page). Still in post as far as checked: Wikipedia describes him as Chanel's creative director and NOWFASHION lists Chanel SS27 on 5 Oct 2026 (designer not named there).

Tenure began before 2012 and ran into the window. Appointment announced 2011-05-09 to succeed Hannah MacGibbon, effective 2011-06-01 (FashionNetwork; The Fashion Spot, both 2011-05-09). First show SS12, Paris, Monday 2011-10-03 (AP via Global News). Chloé confirmed her exit on Monday 2017-01-30, leaving on 2017-03-31 (FashionUnited); last show AW17, Paris, 2017-03-02 (Getty).

Appointment reported 2017-03-10, effective 2017-04-03 (FashionNetwork). First show SS18 at Chloé's Paris headquarters on Thursday morning 2017-09-28 (FashionNetwork, same day). Last show SS21, outdoor show on the Palais de Tokyo steps, 2020-10-01 (Fashion Week Daily diary, 'Day 4: October 1, 2020'). Departure confirmed Thursday 2020-12-03, effective immediately (FashionUnited; Nylon).

Named 2020-12-07, effective immediately (Purseblog and Nylon, both 2020-12-07). First collection AW21, a digital video show shot in Saint-Germain and put online at 13:00 on Wednesday 2021-03-03 during Paris Fashion Week (FashionNetwork). Exit reported by WWD in June 2023 (FashionUnited 2023-06-06) and confirmed by Chloé on 2023-07-06 (FashionUnited; Purseblog). Last show SS24, Paris, Thursday 2023-09-28 (AP via KSAT).

Named on Monday 2023-10-09 (AFP via Malay Mail), which said she would first present a pre-collection in Paris in January 2024 (a trade presentation, not counted as a show). First show AW24, Paris, Thursday 2024-02-29 (AP via News4Jax). Still in post: SS27 was scheduled in Paris on 2026-10-01 (Sky TG24 calendar) and reported as designed by Kamali (CNN via KESQ, 2026-10-07).

Dior Homme artistic director. Appointment announcement date not confirmed: a report dated 29 Mar 2007 said LVMH was close to naming him. First collection presented on live models rather than a catwalk, Sunday 1 Jul 2007. Last show AW18 at the Grand Palais Salon d'Honneur; review dated 22 Jan 2018 refers to Saturday's show, i.e. 20 Jan 2018. Exit announced with Kim Jones's appointment on 19 Mar 2018.

Interim studio led by Bill Gaytten after John Galliano's dismissal; in post on 1 Jan 2012. First show is Gaytten's first collection, Couture AW11, Monday 4 Jul 2011 (he took the bow). Last show AW12 ready-to-wear at the Musée Rodin; AFP report published Sunday 4 Mar 2012 says the show was on Friday, i.e. 2 Mar 2012. No appointment announcement; left_announced_date is the day Raf Simons's appointment was announced.

Creative director of Dior women's collections. First show Couture AW12 in a flower-filled hôtel particulier, Monday 2 Jul 2012. Last show SS16 ready-to-wear, Cour Carrée du Louvre, Friday 2 Oct 2015. Exit announced Thursday 22 Oct 2015.

Interim studio led by Serge Ruffieux and Lucie Meier after Raf Simons. First show Couture SS16, Monday 25 Jan 2016 (timetable plus review). Last show Couture AW16, Monday 4 Jul 2016. No appointment announcement; left_announced_date is the day Maria Grazia Chiuri's appointment was announced.
Artistic director of Dior women's collections. First show SS17, Friday 30 Sep 2016. Last show Cruise 2026 at Villa Albani Torlonia, Rome, 27 May 2025. Dior confirmed her exit on Thursday 29 May 2025.

Dior Homme (later Dior Men) artistic director. First show at the Garde Républicaine barracks, Saturday 23 Jun 2018. Last show AW25 at the Ecole Militaire, Friday 24 Jan 2025. Exit announced Friday 31 Jan 2025.

First womenswear show; menswear debut earlier. Named creative director of Dior men's collections on 17 Apr 2025; first Dior Men show (SS26) Friday 27 Jun 2025, Paris. Named creative director of women's, men's and haute couture on 2 Jun 2025. First womenswear show SS26, Jardin des Tuileries, Wednesday 1 Oct 2025. Still in post: showed SS27 on Tuesday 29 Sep 2026.

Founders; tenure predates the window and creative leadership did not change 2012 to 2026, so all date fields are blank by design. Stefano Gabbana stepped down as chairman (effective 2026-01-01, reported 2026-04-10; Alfonso Dolce took the chair) but keeps his creative role and continues to shape collections with Domenico Dolce (Irish News; The Peninsula). SS27 was on the Milan calendar for 2026-09-26 (Fashion Week Daily).

Founder; tenure predates the window. Announced his departure by letter on Tuesday 2024-03-19 (Fashionista). Final show, his 150th, was the SS25 menswear show at the Babcock factory, La Courneuve, Paris, Saturday 2024-06-22 (Getty; AP via ABC News). His last womenswear show was AW24 in early 2024 (date not checked).

Fashionista reported on 2024-03-19 that a studio team would handle SS25 womenswear. That SS25 womenswear runway show, Paris, 2024-09-25 (Getty), was designed by the studio team and reportedly approved piece by piece by Van Noten (FashionUnited 2024-09-26). Interim ended when Julian Klausner was named (2024-12-09).

Named creative director of the women's and men's collections, reported 2024-12-09 (Fashion Week Daily; FashionUnited; Puig release, undated). His first collection was the Winter 2025 menswear, released as a lookbook shot by Willy Vanderperre on 2025-01-23 (AnOther), not counted as a show. First runway show AW25 womenswear, Opéra Garnier, Paris, Wednesday 2025-03-05 (AP via News4Jax). Still in post: SS27, shown in Paris on Wednesday 2026-09-30, reviewed as his (FashionNetwork 2026-10-01).

Artistic director of menswear and accessories since before 2012 (Fashionista: 'originally creative directing accessories and menswear'); start date not confirmed, left blank. Last standalone menswear show SS25, Milan, 15 Jun 2024 (NOWFASHION); after that menswear was shown in co-ed shows, the last under her being SS26, Milan, 24 Sep 2025. Menswear passed to Maria Grazia Chiuri (appointed October 2025, exact date not confirmed). Wikipedia cites a WWD report of 29 Sep 2025 naming her honorary president.

Long-serving creative director of Fendi womenswear; appointment and first show dates not confirmed, left blank. Died 19 Feb 2019 (FashionNetwork); left_announced_date is the date of his death. Last show AW19, Milan, 21 Feb 2019, two days after his death (NOWFASHION).

Artistic director of womenswear, couture and fur, alongside his Dior Men role. Appointment announced September 2020 and exit announced October 2024 (Wikipedia; exact dates not confirmed, left blank; the appointment citations, WWD per English Wikipedia and Corriere della Sera per Italian Wikipedia, are both dated 9 Sep 2020 but could not be read). First collection was Couture SS21 in Paris in late January 2021, exact date not confirmed (NOWFASHION's 29 Jan 2021 09:32 GMT looks like a gallery timestamp), so first_show_date is blank; first ready-to-wear show AW21, Milan, 24 Feb 2021 (NOWFASHION). Last show SS25, Milan, Tuesday 17 Sep 2024, 15:00 (The Impression calendar; NOWFASHION).

Interim womenswear lead after Lagerfeld's death; she remained artistic director of accessories and menswear (see her menswear row). No formal appointment announcement found; Italian Wikipedia says she took over both men's and women's collections on Lagerfeld's death, 19 Feb 2019. First womenswear show SS20, Milan, Thursday 19 Sep 2019 (Fashionista; NOWFASHION). Last womenswear show before Kim Jones: SS21, Milan, 23 Sep 2020 (NOWFASHION). Kim Jones's appointment was announced in September 2020 (Wikipedia, citing WWD); exact date not confirmed, so left_announced_date is blank.

Second interim period after Kim Jones's exit (Wikipedia: she resumed oversight of women's alongside accessories and menswear). No appointment announcement found. Shows were co-ed: AW25, Milan, Wednesday 26 Feb 2025, 19:30, and SS26, Milan, Wednesday 24 Sep 2025, 14:00 (The Impression calendars; NOWFASHION); a schedule report of 2 Aug 2025 says SS26 was led by her. Maria Grazia Chiuri was appointed in October 2025 (Wikipedia, citing Elle 14 Oct 2025); exact date not confirmed, so left_announced_date is blank.

Chief creative officer; men's and women's both under her (The Impression). Appointed October 2025 (Wikipedia); exact announcement date not confirmed, left blank. First show AW26, co-ed, Milan, 25 Feb 2026 (NOWFASHION; The Impression review names her). Still in post: NOWFASHION lists Couture AW26 (Rome, 9 Jul 2026) and SS27 (Milan, 23 Sep 2026), and LVMH posted a Fendi SS27 item on 25 Sep 2026.

Creative director from February 2005 (Wikipedia); start dates not filled. Last womenswear show SS17, Paris, 2 Oct 2016; last show overall menswear AW17, Bibliothèque nationale de France, Paris, 20 Jan 2017 (both NOWFASHION, which names him). Exit announced February 2017 (Wikipedia, citing a Guardian report of 2 Feb 2017); exact date not confirmed, left blank. No Givenchy show between his exit and Clare Waight Keller's debut was found (NOWFASHION lists no AW17 womenswear show).

Artistic director, women's and men's. Appointment announced March 2017 and exit April 2020 (Wikipedia, citing Vogue of 16 Mar 2017 and the Guardian of 10 Apr 2020); exact dates not confirmed, left blank. First show SS18, Paris, 1 Oct 2017 (NOWFASHION names her). Last show AW20 womenswear, Paris, 1 Mar 2020 (NOWFASHION); her last couture show was SS20 on 21 Jan 2020 and last menswear show AW20 on 16 Jan 2020 (NOWFASHION).

Creative director, women's and men's, June 2020 to 1 Jan 2024 (Wikipedia); appointment and exit announcement dates not confirmed (Wikipedia gives June 2020 and November 2023, its sources date from 15 Jun 2020 and 1 Dec 2023), left blank. First show SS21, Paris, 4 Oct 2020 (NOWFASHION, designer not named; attribution inferred from timing). Last show SS24 womenswear, Paris, 28 Sep 2023 (NOWFASHION; listed in the FHCM SS24 calendar); last menswear show SS24 on 22 Jun 2023 (NOWFASHION).

House design team after Matthew Williams left at the end of 2023 (Hypebeast, 1 Mar 2024). First womenswear show; menswear earlier: the team opened the interim with AW24 menswear in January (NOWFASHION: 17 Jan 2024). Only womenswear show AW24, Paris, 29 Feb 2024 (NOWFASHION); no SS25 show is listed. No appointment announcement; the period ended with Sarah Burton's appointment in September 2024 (exact date not confirmed, so left_announced_date is blank).

Creative director. Appointed September 2024 (Wikipedia; its source is a WWD exclusive of 9 Sep 2024); exact announcement date not confirmed, left blank. First collection shown March 2025 (Wikipedia): AW25, Paris, 7 Mar 2025 (NOWFASHION). Her first menswear look appeared on 2 Mar 2025 at the Academy Awards (Wikipedia); NOWFASHION lists a Givenchy menswear SS27 show on 25 Jun 2026 without naming the designer. No departure found (Wikipedia describes her as current).

Named creative director of womenswear in 2005 (FashionUnited, 16 Jun 2005); John Ray left the menswear post in January 2006 (just-style), and by 2012 she led both lines (Dazed reports the AW15 men's show was overhauled after her exit). Appointment announcement date not confirmed, left blank. First collection as womenswear lead: Cruise 2006 at the Gagosian Gallery, New York; FashionUnited report dated 16 Jun 2005 says it was shown 'yesterday'. Last show SS15 womenswear, Milan, Wednesday 17 Sep 2014. Kering announced her exit on Friday 12 Dec 2014, initially for after the Feb 2015 shows; she left about 9 Jan 2015 and did not show again.

First womenswear show; menswear debut earlier: he took the bow at the AW15 men's show in Milan on 19 Jan 2015, two days before Gucci and Kering announced his appointment (Wednesday 21 Jan 2015). First womenswear show AW15, Milan, Wednesday 25 Feb 2015. Last show SS23 'Twinsburg', Milan, Friday 23 Sep 2022. Exit announced Wednesday 23 Nov 2022.

In-house design team after Michele's exit. First womenswear show; menswear earlier: men's AW23, Milan, Friday 13 Jan 2023 (team took no bows). Womenswear AW23, Milan, Friday 24 Feb 2023. Last show Cruise 2024 at Gyeongbokgung Palace, Seoul, Tuesday 16 May 2023 (livestream notice plus same-day review). Men's SS24 in June 2023 was a presentation by the design team, not a runway; exact date not confirmed. No appointment announcement; left_announced_date is the day Sabato De Sarno's appointment was announced.

Kering announced the appointment on Saturday 28 Jan 2023. First show SS24 ('Ancora'), Milan, Friday 22 Sep 2023; his menswear debut came later (La Conceria calls the 17 Jun 2024 men's show his second; the first was not checked). Last show SS25 womenswear at Triennale Milano, 20 Sep 2024 (Gucci press release); last menswear show SS25 at the Triennale, Monday 17 Jun 2024. Exit announced Thursday 6 Feb 2025; the AW25 show was assigned to the design office.

Gucci design office after De Sarno's exit; co-ed shows. First show AW25, Milan, Tuesday 25 Feb 2025. Last show Cruise 2026 in Florence (Palazzo Settimanni archive), 15 May 2025, credited to the in-house team (local review published 23 May; Milano Finanza same-day notice of the 20:00 show). No appointment announcement; left_announced_date is the day Demna's appointment was announced.

Artistic director. Kering and Gucci announced the appointment on Thursday 13 Mar 2025, effective early July 2025. First collection 'La Famiglia' was released as a digital lookbook on Instagram on Monday 22 Sep 2025 and shown on the red carpet of the Milan premiere of the short film 'The Tiger' on Tuesday 23 Sep 2025; no runway. First runway show AW26, Milan, Friday 27 Feb 2026. Still in post: second runway show SS27, Milan, 25 Sep 2026.

Artistic director of Hermès menswear from 1988 (Wikipedia); start dates not filled. Final show, her 76th, AW26 menswear, Paris, Saturday 24 Jan 2026, 20:00 (Wikipedia; The Impression calendar; NOWFASHION). Her departure was announced in October 2025, a few days before Hermès confirmed Grace Wales Bonner (report of 21 Oct 2025); exact date not confirmed, left blank.

Artistic director of women's ready-to-wear 2010 to 2014 (Wikipedia); announcement and exit dates not confirmed, left blank. Show dates from NOWFASHION, which does not name the designer: AW11, Paris, 6 Mar 2011 (taken as his first) and AW14, Paris, 5 Mar 2014 (taken as his last); attribution inferred from the tenure years, hence verified=false.

Also written Nadège Vanhée-Cybulski. Artistic director of women's ready-to-wear since 2014 (Wikipedia); appointment date not confirmed, left blank. First show taken as SS15, Orangerie du Sénat, Paris, 1 Oct 2014 (NOWFASHION, designer not named; attribution inferred). No departure found: NOWFASHION lists SS27 on 3 Oct 2026.

Creative director of men's ready-to-wear. Announcement date from a blog report of 21 Oct 2025 saying Hermès had confirmed her (Wikipedia also cites a New York Times report of that date), hence verified=false. First collection scheduled for January 2027; not yet shown.

Creative director of women's and men's from 2005 (Wikipedia); start dates not confirmed, left blank. Last collection AW12 (Wikipedia), shown in Milan on 25 Feb 2012 (NOWFASHION). His exit and Jil Sander's return were announced in February 2012, days before that show (Wikipedia); exact date not confirmed, left blank.

Third stint at her label. Return announced February 2012 (Italian Wikipedia cites the Telegraph of 23 Feb 2012) and exit in autumn/October 2013 (Wikipedia); exact dates not confirmed, left blank. First womenswear show; menswear debut earlier: her first collection after the return was menswear SS13, Milan, 23 Jun 2012 (NOWFASHION; Italian Wikipedia: end of June 2012). First womenswear show SS13, Milan, 22 Sep 2012 (NOWFASHION). Last show SS14, Milan, 21 Sep 2013 (NOWFASHION), the last before her October 2013 exit; attribution rests on that exit date.

Interim period between Jil Sander's exit (autumn 2013) and Rodolfo Paglialunga's appointment in April 2014 (Italian Wikipedia, citing TextilWirtschaft of 29 Apr 2014). Its only womenswear show was AW14, Milan, 22 Feb 2014 (NOWFASHION, no designer named). No appointment announcement; the period ended with Paglialunga's appointment, whose exact date was not confirmed, so left_announced_date is blank.

Creative director 2014 to 2017. Appointed April 2014 (Italian Wikipedia, citing TextilWirtschaft of 29 Apr 2014) and left in spring 2017 (citing Vogue Germany of 15 Mar 2017); exact dates not confirmed, left blank. First show taken as SS15, Milan, 20 Sep 2014, the first Jil Sander show after his appointment (NOWFASHION does not name the designer), hence verified=false. Last show not confirmed: AW17, Milan, 25 Feb 2017 if he was still in post, otherwise SS17, 24 Sep 2016 (both NOWFASHION); whether AW17 was his or a studio collection was not established, so no 2017 design-studio row was added. Scope given as womenswear; not confirmed.

Co-creative directors. Appointed April 2017 (Italian Wikipedia, citing Die Welt of 7 Apr 2017); exact announcement date not confirmed, left blank. First show SS18, Milan, 23 Sep 2017 (NOWFASHION), the first show after their appointment. Last show AW25, Milan, Wednesday 26 Feb 2025, 10:30; the brand announced the end of their tenure a few hours after the show (Hypebeast; The Impression calendar).

Formerly creative director of Bally. Appointed spring 2025 (Wikipedia cites a BoF report dated 10 Mar 2025); exact announcement date not confirmed, left blank. First show SS26, co-ed, Milan, Wednesday 24 Sep 2025, 10:30 (The Impression calendar; Vogue Philippines schedule names it his debut; NOWFASHION). No departure found: NOWFASHION lists SS27 on 23 Sep 2026.

Creative director from January 2008; his move from Mulberry was reported 27 Jul 2007 (exact announcement date not confirmed, left blank). First Loewe catwalk show was AW09 in Paris in the week before 10 Mar 2009 (exact date not confirmed, left blank); earlier collections were not shown on a catwalk. Last show AW13, Paris, 2 Mar 2013 (NOWFASHION). Coach announced his hiring on Monday 24 Jun 2013 (FashionNetwork, published 25 Jun). No Loewe runway show was found between his exit and Anderson's first collection (27 Jun 2014): Modaes (28 Jun 2013) reported SS14 might go unshown and FashionNetwork (3 Apr 2014) says Loewe sat out an autumn/winter Paris season, so no design-studio row was added.

Appointed alongside LVMH's minority stake in J.W. Anderson; Fashion Week Daily reported the confirmation on 25 Sep 2013 (FashionUnited and The Guardian covered it on 26 Sep). First womenswear show; menswear debut earlier: first menswear collection presented at Loewe's new Paris headquarters, rue Bonaparte, Friday 27 Jun 2014. First womenswear show SS15 in the UNESCO gardens, Paris, Friday 26 Sep 2014. Last collection AW25, a co-ed presentation (not a runway) in Karl Lagerfeld's former home, rue de l'Université, Monday 10 Mar 2025 (FHCM calendar, 09:00 to 18:00). Loewe confirmed his exit on Monday 17 Mar 2025.

Proenza Schouler founders; co-creative directors. Loewe announced on Monday 24 Mar 2025; tenure began 7 Apr 2025. First show SS26, Paris, 3 Oct 2025 (NOWFASHION gives the date; Wikipedia identifies SS26 as their first collection). Still in post: their second show (AW26) was reviewed on 6 Mar 2026 and LVMH posted 'Ease and presence for Loewe Spring-Summer 2027' on 5 Oct 2026.

No named creative director found for Loro Piana; collections are credited to the house. Examples: SS26 co-ed show at Palazzo Citterio, Milan, reviewed 2025-09-24 with no designer named (FashionNetwork); AW26 presented at the Brera headquarters by product developers Nicola Salin and Alessandra Varianini (FashionNetwork 2026-03-01). Frédéric Arnault became CEO in 2025, a business role (FashionNetwork 2025-03-12). The position for 2012 to 2024 was not confirmed from a source read (web search budget ran out), hence verified false.

Artistic director from 1997 (Wikipedia); start dates not filled. Last show SS14, Cour Carrée du Louvre, Paris, 2 Oct 2013, described by NOWFASHION as his final show for the house. Departure announcement date not confirmed, left blank.

Men's style director (later men's artistic director) from early 2011; appointment date not confirmed, left blank. First show SS12, Paris, 23 Jun 2011, and last show AW18, Paris, 18 Jan 2018 (both NOWFASHION, which names him; the AW18 finale featured Kate Moss and Naomi Campbell). Exit announcement date 17 Jan 2018, the day before that show, is from Wikipedia only.

Artistic director of women's collections. Appointment date from Wikipedia only ('On 4 November 2013, the company confirmed...', citing WWD). First show AW14, Paris, 5 Mar 2014 (NOWFASHION names him). Still in post: The Impression's review of SS27 names him; NOWFASHION lists the show on 6 Oct 2026.

Men's artistic director. Appointment date from Wikipedia only: the Louis Vuitton article says 26 Mar 2018 and the Abloh article says 25 Mar 2018 (both citing a New York Times report dated 26 Mar). First show SS19, Palais-Royal gardens, Paris, 21 Jun 2018 (NOWFASHION; Wikipedia). Died 28 Nov 2021 (Wikipedia); left_announced_date is the date of death. last_show_date is AW22, Paris, 20 Jan 2022 (NOWFASHION date), shown after his death; that it was his final collection is not confirmed by a source read here. Men's studio after Abloh's death; NOWFASHION credits both collections to the house, not a named designer. First show SS23, Paris, 23 Jun 2022; last show AW23, Paris, 19 Jan 2023. No appointment announcement; left_announced_date is the day Pharrell Williams was named, from Wikipedia only.

Men's creative director. Appointment date from Wikipedia only (both the Pharrell Williams and Louis Vuitton articles give 14 Feb 2023). First show SS24, Paris, 20 Jun 2023 (NOWFASHION listing; Wikipedia says his first show was in June 2023). No departure found: Wikipedia describes him as current and NOWFASHION lists men's SS27 on 23 Jun 2026 (designer not named there).

In-house design team with no named creative director (OTB's chairman calls Glenn Martens only the third creative director in the house's history, per Wikipedia); in post on 1 Jan 2012; start dates not filled. Last womenswear show SS15, Paris, 26 Sep 2014 (NOWFASHION). A menswear AW15 show followed on 23 Jan 2015 (NOWFASHION, designer not named; attribution not confirmed). left_announced_date is the day OTB announced John Galliano, from Wikipedia only.

Creative director. Appointment (OTB announcement, 6 Oct 2014) and first show (Artisanal couture collection during London Collections: Men, 12 Jan 2015) are from Wikipedia only. First ready-to-wear show AW15, Grand Palais, Paris, 6 Mar 2015 (NOWFASHION). Last show taken as the Artisanal 2024 couture show, Paris, 25 Jan 2024 (NOWFASHION), the last Margiela show NOWFASHION lists before Glenn Martens. Exit announced December 2024 (Wikipedia cites The Independent, 12 Dec 2024); exact date not confirmed, left blank.

Appointed January 2025 (Wikipedia); exact announcement date not confirmed, left blank. First show Artisanal couture AW25, Paris, Wednesday 9 Jul 2025, 19:30 (The Impression calendar; an AFP preview of 8 Jul 2025 places his first Margiela collection after Demna's Balenciaga farewell that Wednesday). First ready-to-wear show SS26, Paris, 4 Oct 2025 (NOWFASHION). No departure found: the house site lists an SS27 show on 29 Sep 2026.

Max Mara is designed by an in-house team led by Ian Griffiths, credited as creative director in a September 2014 show report (FashionUnited 2014-09-18) and for AW26 (FashionNetwork 2026-02-27). The date he took the title, and so whether he led the line in January 2012, was not confirmed from a source read (web search budget ran out), hence verified false. Wikipedia lists Laura Lusuardi as design director, without dates. Shows are in Milan (SS27 on 2026-09-24 per Fashion Week Daily) and resort shows elsewhere.

Founder-led line; no change of creative lead found 2012 to 2026, so all date fields are blank by design. Still in post: SS27 shown in Paris on 2026-10-04 (FHCM collection page) and reviewed as 'Miuccia Prada's Miu Miu SS27' (nss magazine 2026-10-05). Dario Vitale, who left for Versace in 2025, had been Miu Miu's design and image director, not its creative lead (Capri Holdings release 2025-03-13).

Founder-led; sole creative lead of the Prada women's and men's lines from before 2012, so announced and first-show dates are left blank. Not a departure: left_announced_date is 2020-02-23, when Prada announced Raf Simons as co-creative director with equal responsibilities, effective 2020-04-02 (Prada press release); she continues as co-creative director (next row). last_show_date is her last solo collection, 'Multiple Views' SS21 (men's and women's), streamed during Milan Digital Fashion Week on 2020-07-14 (Harper's Bazaar SG: 'July 14, 8pm Singapore time'; FashionUnited 2020-07-15).

Co-creative directors 'with equal responsibilities for creative input and decision-making', effective 2020-04-02 (Prada press release dated 2020-02-23). First joint collection SS21 womenswear, shown as a digital film during Milan Fashion Week on Thursday 2020-09-24 (AP via Click2Houston). Still in post: credited jointly for AW26 (FashionNetwork 2026-02-27) and for SS27, shown in Milan on 2026-09-22 (Stylerave 2026-09-23).

Creative director of Yves Saint Laurent from 2004, succeeding Tom Ford; designed women's and men's. Gucci Group announced the appointment in March 2004 but the sources read disagree on the day (Hello! item dated 2004-03-10; FashionUnited 2004-03-12 says 'Thursday', i.e. 2004-03-11), so announced_date is blank. First show (October 2004) predates the window and was not checked. PPR confirmed his exit on 2012-02-28; final show AW12 womenswear, Paris, 2012-03-05 (FashionUnited; AP via Washington Times, Monday 2012-03-05).

Appointment confirmed 2012-03-07, overseeing men's and women's (Out, citing WWD and CEO Paul Deneve); WWD expected a first collection for resort in June 2012, but no resort show was checked, so the SS13 runway is used. First show SS13 womenswear, Paris, 2012-10-01 (NOWFASHION show page; Daily Beast review published the same day). Menswear debut AW13, reported 2013-01-20 (Fox News). Last show AW16, Paris, 2016-03-07 (Dazed, 2016-03-08: 'last night's show'). Departure announced Friday 2016-04-01 (FashionUnited).

Named creative director 'with immediate effect' by Kering on Monday 2016-04-04 (ANSA; FashionNetwork). First show SS17, Paris, Tuesday 2016-09-27 (AP caption via Gulf News). Still in post as of 2026-10-07: press reports and the show notes suggested SS27 (Paris, 2026-09-29) was his last show, but Saint Laurent and Kering had not confirmed a departure (FashionUnited 2026-09-29; Dazed 2026-09-30; CNN via KESQ 2026-10-07), so last_show_date and left_announced_date are blank.

Founder; menswear and the 2010 womenswear relaunch both predate the window. Last runway show SS23, New York Fashion Week, Skylight on Vesey, 2022-09-14 (Getty). His final collection, AW23 'Tom Ford Archive', was released on the brand's website on Wednesday 2023-04-26 with a video and no show (FashionUnited 2023-04-27); lookbook or online releases are not counted as shows in this file. Estée Lauder agreed to buy the brand in November 2022; on completion, 2023-04-28, it announced Ford moving to an adviser role and Peter Hawkings succeeding him as creative director (ELC release). Zegna Group became the fashion licensee the same day (Zegna release).

Named creative director for womenswear, menswear and accessories on 2023-04-28, effective at the closing of the Estée Lauder deal (ELC release); previously SVP of Tom Ford menswear. Debut SS24, Milan, Thursday 2023-09-21 (AFP via Malay Mail; W). Last show AW24, Milan, 2024-02-22 (Getty caption via Grazia MY). Departure announced 2024-07-22 (Tom Ford release on Business Wire).

Interim after Hawkings's exit (announced 2024-07-22) until Haider Ackermann was named on 2024-09-04. The SS25 collection was presented only in the Milan showroom in September 2024, with no runway (Business Wire release), so first_show_date is blank; the sources read do not say who designed it. Ackermann's first collection followed in March 2025.

Named creative director 2024-09-04 (FashionUnited). Debut AW25, Pavillon Vendôme, Paris, Wednesday night 2025-03-05 (FashionNetwork and W, both 2025-03-06). Still in post: Zegna Group's chairman cited his Paris show in March 2026 (FashionUnited 2026-03-20) and SS27, shown in Paris on 2026-09-30, is credited to him (W, updated 2026-10-06; CNN via KESQ).

Departure announced Friday 2024-03-22 (AFP via Malay Mail; FashionUnited); Valentino then cancelled its June 2024 men's and couture shows (FashionUnited 2024-03-26).

Named creative director, based in Rome, on Thursday 2024-03-28 (AP via WSLS). First runway show SS25, Pavillon des Folies, Paris, Sunday 2024-09-29 (L'Officiel USA). Creative head of Versace from 1997 (pre-window; appointment date and first show not checked). Last show AW25, Milan, Friday 2025-02-28 (AP captions via ClickOnDetroit). Chief Creative Officer effective 2025-04-01 (Capri Holdings release 2025-03-13); joined from Miu Miu. His only collection, SS26, was presented at an 'intimate event' at the Pinacoteca Ambrosiana, Milan, on Friday 2025-09-26 (AP via WSLS), so first and last show coincide. Exit announced 2025-12-04, effective 2025-12-12, two days after Prada Group closed its acquisition of Versace (Dazed).

Interim between Vitale's exit and Pieter Mulier's start on 2026-07-01; announced_date is the date Vitale's exit was announced (no separate interim announcement found). No show in this period: Versace was absent from the Milan calendar for SS27 'for the second season in a row', i.e. also AW26 (Fashion Week Daily 2026-07-30). The AW26 collection and campaign were not attributed to any designer (Dazed 2026-07-30). Ended when Mulier was named on 2026-02-05 (FashionUnited).

Named Chief Creative Officer on 2026-02-05, effective 2026-07-01 (FashionUnited); first day in the office was 2026-07-01 (Dazed). No collection shown as of 2026-10-07: Versace skipped the SS27 Milan calendar and his runway debut is planned for February 2027, i.e. AW27 in Milan (Dazed and Fashion Week Daily, both 2026-07-30), so first_show_date is blank. Came from Alaïa (see alaia rows).

Placeholder for the Ermenegildo Zegna main line before Stefano Pilati, who took charge of the brand's fashion show and Couture collection from 2013-01-01 and first showed in June 2013 (FashionUnited 2012-09-05), so the January 2012, June 2012 and January 2013 shows preceded him. Head of design at Ermenegildo Zegna (fashion show and Couture collection) and creative director of Agnona, announced by a Zegna Group statement in early September 2012 (FashionUnited report dated 2012-09-05); the exact day was not confirmed, so announced_date is blank. Started 2013-01-01. First show SS14, Milan, 2013-06-22 (NOWFASHION show page; single source). He announced his exit on Wednesday 2016-02-03 (FashionUnited; Fashionista); his final men's collection was shown in Milan in January 2016, exact date not confirmed, so last_show_date is blank.

Gap between Pilati's exit (announced 2016-02-03) and Alessandro Sartori's start in June 2016; Sartori was named 2016-02-05 and his first full collection was AW17, January 2017 (FashionUnited; LUXUO). Whether a SS17 collection was shown in June 2016, and who designed it, was not confirmed.

Named to the newly created role of artistic director for all Zegna brands on 2016-02-05, starting June 2016 (FashionUnited; LUXUO). First show was the Ermenegildo Zegna Couture AW17 collection at HangarBicocca, Milan, in January 2017 (Wikipedia; FashionUnited said his first full collection would be shown in Milan in January 2017); the exact day was not confirmed, so first_show_date is blank. Had been creative director of Z Zegna from 2003, then at Berluti.
